title: A menu with clear constraints
description: Matching meals against saved conditions and checking the ingredients, without quietly relaxing the exclusions.

blocks.text: A family sets the conditions for the menu, then swaps out one dinner that does not suit. The app keeps the rest of the settings and shows why the replacement was suggested before recalculating the shopping.

quote.text: I put in my macros targets for keto and it said I was outside of their “recommended range” for fat so it didn’t give me any meals. Pretty much useless unless your macros fall inside their “recommended range”.

blocks.text: Swapping a meal without losing the conditions

Numeric targets, tastes and excluded ingredients have to be told apart. When a set of conditions is not supported, a person needs a specific answer and a way to revise it; quietly relaxing the exclusions is not acceptable.

The reviews confirm that the matching is convenient and that an unexplained refusal is irritating, but not that any given diet is sound. The first version is worth limiting to a clear set of recipes with ingredients that can be checked, with no promises about health outcomes.
